summary: [Digital Liberia 2025-2029](2026-02-03 Liberia Unveils 5-Year 'Digital Liberia' Strategy to Boost Sovereignty and Innovation) was published in February 2026 on eight priority areas across four pillars, with no costing or delivery schedule.
developments:
The pillars include universal connectivity, digital addressing, cybersecurity and data sovereignty, replacing an ICT policy already past its stated period ([strategy](2026-02-03 Liberia Unveils 5-Year 'Digital Liberia' Strategy to Boost Sovereignty and Innovation), [text](2026-02-03 Liberia National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 (Digital Liberia))).

A development bank's country strategy approved the same month still cites the superseded 2019-2024 ICT policy and does not mention the new strategy at all ([country strategy](2026-07-31-liberia-afdb-country-strategy-paper-2026-2031)).
qualifier: Digital Liberia 2025-2029 published; no costing, delivery schedule or progress report on record

summary: A [licensing and spectrum reform package](2026-07-17-lta-telecom-reforms-star-cell-revoked-fpa) was announced in July 2026, splitting infrastructure and service licences and promising first satellite rules.
developments:
It also carries tower-sharing rules, a device-identity regime and repatriation of the country-code domain; none has been published as an instrument ([reform package](2026-07-17-lta-telecom-reforms-star-cell-revoked-fpa)).

Licensing has otherwise run unchanged under a 2007 statute with no satellite or device rules, so the package would be the first structural change to the market's licensing in nineteen years.
qualifier: regulator's own 2025-2029 plan in abridged form; no implementation reporting against it on record

summary: No separately titled broadband strategy; the [January 2026 infrastructure roadmap](2026-04-08-liberia-national-infrastructure-conference-2026-report) commits the ministry and the regulator to one in years 2-4.
developments:
The broadband and universal-access targets sat in the [National ICT Policy 2019-2024](2019-10-31-liberia-mopt-national-ict-policy-2019-2024), whose stated period expired in 2024 and which the repository holds no successor to. The [2026-2029 roadmap](2026-04-08-liberia-national-infrastructure-conference-2026-report) adopted after the national infrastructure conference of 19-23 January 2026 places a national broadband expansion plan in years 2-4, which is a commitment to draft rather than a plan.

The repository holds no costing, no coverage target and no delivery schedule for that plan.
qualifier: no broadband plan; roadmap commits ministry and regulator to prepare one in years 2-4

summary: A [cloud-first policy and a government network](2026-04-08-liberia-national-infrastructure-conference-2026-report) are named in the 2026-2029 infrastructure roadmap, with no instrument or timetable behind them.
developments:
The [infrastructure roadmap](2026-04-08-liberia-national-infrastructure-conference-2026-report) adopted in 2026 names a cloud-first policy and a government network among its digital commitments. Nothing published sets out what would be hosted where, under whose standards, or by when.

The repository holds no government cloud policy, no hosting standard and no migration plan; the nearest binding rule is sectoral, the [central bank's requirement](2020-01-08-liberia-cbl-e-payment-services-regulations-2020) that payment systems be hosted locally.
qualifier: cloud-first named in infrastructure roadmap; no instrument or timetable

summary: [Executive Order 163](2026-04-28-liberia-executive-order-163-otdi-national-digitalization) requires a first release of a Government Interoperability Framework within 180 days; none is published.
developments:
[Executive Order 163](2026-04-28-liberia-executive-order-163-otdi-national-digitalization), signed 22 April 2026, creates the Office of Technology, Digitalization and Innovation as the central authority for government-wide technical standards and sets a 180-day deadline for a first release of the framework, alongside an enterprise architecture framework and a digital systems inventory.

The [terms of reference](2026-07-17-liberia-otdi-terms-of-reference-executive-order-163) for the office's chief technology officer, published in July 2026, assign the duty to develop and maintain the framework with its data-exchange standards. Neither the framework nor a draft of it has been published.
qualifier: framework mandated by Executive Order 163; nothing published by the as-at

summary: An [artificial intelligence priority was accepted in principle](2026-07-29-fpa-youth-manifesto-ai-boakai) by the President in July 2026, conditioned on agriculture, transport and commerce applications.
developments:
No policy, institution, budget line or date is attached, and the proposal came from the President's youth advisory council rather than from the executive ([acceptance](2026-07-29-fpa-youth-manifesto-ai-boakai)).

It is the only statement of national intent on the technology the repository holds, and it originated outside government.
qualifier: AI priority accepted in principle only; no drafting, task force or strategy section on record

summary: [Section 9(c) of the 2020 payment regulations](2020-01-08-liberia-cbl-e-payment-services-regulations-2020) is the only localisation rule, and it carries an offshore escape clause.
developments:
The [regulations](2020-01-08-liberia-cbl-e-payment-services-regulations-2020) gazetted 8 January 2020 state that a licensee's payment system should be hosted locally, and that where it is hosted abroad the licensee must supply requested information promptly and give the central bank unfettered access.

That is a sectoral norm with an escape, not an economy-wide regime. The repository holds no general data-localisation instrument, and the National Data Policy that might carry one was still [in multi-stakeholder drafting](2025-11-14-liberia-national-data-policy-multistakeholder-consultation-au) in November 2025.
qualifier: sectoral payment-system hosting rule with offshore escape; no category-based regime

summary: A [national data governance policy](2026-03-01-liberia-national-data-governance-policy) issued in March 2026 designates the information commission as data regulator and sets an adequacy-or-consent rule for transfers.
developments:
It prescribes signature and ratification of the continental cyber and data convention, and was developed under ministry leadership with a regional civil-society body and aligned to the continental data policy framework ([policy](2026-03-01-liberia-national-data-governance-policy)).

It designates a regulator under a statute that was unenacted when the policy issued, so the policy named an authority for a law that did not yet exist; the law has since been signed and the authority still has not been constituted.
qualifier: final policy issued March 2026; no implementing instruments on record

summary: No adopted open-data policy; the statistics office publishes [public-use microdata](2026-02-01-liberia-lisgis-wen-survey-2024-public-use-dataset) under access conditions instead.
developments:
The [anonymised public-use dataset](2026-02-01-liberia-lisgis-wen-survey-2024-public-use-dataset) for the 2024 women's empowerment and nutrition survey was released on the statistics office's own microdata portal under stated access conditions, with the confidentiality basis cited as the [2004 statistics Act](2004-07-01-liberia-national-statistics-and-geo-information-act-2004) rather than an open-data instrument.

That is open-data practice in the absence of a policy. The repository holds no adopted national open data policy and no government open-data licence.
qualifier: statistics office publishes microdata under the statistics Act; no open-data instrument adopted

summary: The [Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act has been in force since its printing on 23 March 2026](2026-03-23-liberia-data-protection-act-printed-act-mopt), five months before its announced signing, with no commissioner yet appointed under it.
developments:
It reached a House committee in June 2025 ([committee stage](2025-06-11-house-reviews-privacy-data-protection-bill-observer)). The [printed Act shows approval on 9 March 2026 and effect on publication on 23 March, gives an Independent Information Commissioner 24 months for implementing rules and existing businesses a year's transition](2026-03-23-liberia-data-protection-act-printed-act-mopt); a [ministerial announcement of 19 August presented it as newly signed](2026-08-20-wearetech-liberia-cybercrime-data-protection-laws).

No commissioner appointment, rule or registration regime under it is held, so what a data subject can do with it is still unestablished ([enforcement position](2025-02-27 Liberia struggles to enforce privacy and data protection laws)).

2026-09-14 — the first test of the new law was a government leak: the ministry [confirmed that beneficiary records circulating on social media are authentic and their disclosure unauthorised](2026-09-14-smartnewsliberia-mgcsp-beneficiary-data-leak-investigation), and opened an internal investigation. No regulator action is held.
qualifier: Act in force March 2026; no commissioner appointment or implementing rules on record

summary: The [Cybercrime Act was approved on 3 July and printed on 24 July 2026](2026-07-24-liberia-cybercrime-act-2025-printed-act-mopt), six weeks before its announced signing, alongside [sector cybersecurity regulations](2026-01-13-liberia-lta-cybersecurity-regulations-reg-0013-2026) already in force.
developments:
The [printed Act creates a National Cybersecurity Council with the national CERT as technical arm and a 72-hour breach report to it](2026-07-24-liberia-cybercrime-act-2025-printed-act-mopt); an international index still places the country in its second-lowest maturity tier ([enactment](2026-08-20-tech-africa-liberia-enacts-cybercrime-data-protection-laws)).

The regulator's own 2026 regulations require telecom providers to store personal data primarily inside the country, notify the regulator of breaches within 24 hours and customers within 72, and keep security-event logs for at least twelve months; penalties apply only from a year after the effective date ([regulations](2026-01-13-liberia-lta-cybersecurity-regulations-reg-0013-2026)).

A National Cybersecurity Act scheduled for the third quarter of 2025 by the strategy's own action plan is not held as a draft, bill or enactment ([action plan](2024-07-01-liberia-national-cybersecurity-strategy-2025-2029)).

2026-09-19 - the Act entered its enforcement phase: [the Executive Protection Service's director warned that manipulated material could bring prosecution under it](2026-09-19-lbr-smartnewsliberia-cybercrime-act-free-speech), and [police confirmed that a man held over AI-generated images of the Vice-President was arrested under the Act; the Vice-President asked for his release and said he would not press charges](2026-09-21-lbr-newdawn-koung-seeks-release-ai-image-suspect). On 22 September a court [freed him on habeas corpus, and the main opposition party said it would ask the Supreme Court to rule on the Act](2026-09-23-lbr-fpa-cdc-cybercrime-law-supreme-court); no court has ruled on the offence.
qualifier: Act in force July 2026; no regulations under it or prosecution on record by the as-at

summary: The [2011 Act](2011-08-08-liberia-national-identification-registry-act-2011) is the enacting statute for the biometric register and remains unamended.
developments:
The [National Identification Registry Act](2011-08-08-liberia-national-identification-registry-act-2011), approved 1 August 2011, repeals the earlier decree, creates the autonomous registry, and makes the National Biometric Identification System, the biometric card and the Social Security Number the primary government identity number.

What has moved since is executive rather than legislative: [Executive Order 147](2025-04-01-liberia-executive-order-147-mandatory-nbis-enrollment) of April 2025 compels enrolment and verification, with data handling bound back to Part IX of the same Act. No amending statute is on the record.
qualifier: 2011 Act in force establishing the registry; regulations and grievance provisions not on record

summary: The [mobile money regulations](2024-01-01 Liberia Mobile Money Regulations (Central Bank of Liberia)) are in force and unamended, and the interoperable fee schedule of 2026 was approved under them.
developments:
They are the central bank's standing mobile-money framework ([regulations](2024-01-01 Liberia Mobile Money Regulations (Central Bank of Liberia))).

No payments statute, electronic transactions act or switch instrument sits above them, so a fee schedule for a national instant payment system rests on a regulation written before that system existed.
qualifier: mobile money regulations in force; licensing and interoperability provisions not shown in rows

summary: [Executive Order 147](2025-04-01-liberia-executive-order-147-mandatory-nbis-enrollment) compels inter-agency verification against the identity register; no statute enables data exchange generally.
developments:
[Executive Order 147](2025-04-01-liberia-executive-order-147-mandatory-nbis-enrollment) requires all public and private institutions to use the registry database, the Identity Query Portal and the e-Verification platform, which is the only operative instrument compelling data sharing across Liberian agencies.

It is an executive order resting on the [2011 Act](2011-08-08-liberia-national-identification-registry-act-2011), not a data-exchange statute. [Executive Order 163](2026-04-28-liberia-executive-order-163-otdi-national-digitalization) of April 2026 mandates a Government Interoperability Framework but is likewise executive.
qualifier: executive order requires verification against the registry; no implementing acts or custodian

summary: No artificial-intelligence instrument: a court reached [alleged AI-generated audio](2025-12-22-liberia-criminal-court-a-ai-generated-voice-recording-evidence-newdawn) through ordinary disclosure rules.
developments:
At Criminal Court A on 19 December 2025 the defence [played an alleged AI-generated recording](2025-12-22-liberia-criminal-court-a-ai-generated-voice-recording-evidence-newdawn) to argue that social-media audio is inadmissible without forensic corroboration; the judge sustained the objection on disclosure grounds, applying no AI-specific rule because none exists in the reported reasoning.

The executive's own response to synthetic media is an appeal rather than a rule: in July 2026 the presidential press secretary [warned of fabricated and AI-generated documents](2026-07-16-liberia-emansion-ai-generated-documents-warning-frontpage-africa) attributed to government and asked citizens to authenticate through official channels.
qualifier: searched absence: no AI-specific instrument or evidentiary rule

summary: The [2002 Electronic Transactions Law](2002-06-19-liberia-electronic-transactions-law-chapter-13-title-14) is the only enacted e-commerce statute and predates platforms entirely.
developments:
Chapter 13 of Title 14, [approved 8 January 2002 and published 19 June 2002](2002-06-19-liberia-electronic-transactions-law-chapter-13-title-14), facilitates the use of electronic transactions for commercial purposes.

Nothing covering online consumer protection, platform obligations or intermediary liability has been enacted in the twenty-four years since. The repository holds no e-commerce bill in drafting.
qualifier: 2002 Electronic Transactions Law; no online consumer protection or trust-service rules since

summary: The [2004 Act](2004-07-01-liberia-national-statistics-and-geo-information-act-2004) stands unamended, and was tested in the House in [June 2026](2026-06-29-liberia-hor-summons-nec-lisgis-constitutional-threshold).
developments:
The [National Statistics and Geo-Information Act](2004-07-01-liberia-national-statistics-and-geo-information-act-2004), approved 22 July 2004, creates the statistics office as an autonomous agency, empowers it to demand information from any ministry, bureau or agency, and binds its staff to an oath of confidentiality.

No amendment moved in the window. What did move is a test of the statutory role: in [June 2026 the House summoned](2026-06-29-liberia-hor-summons-nec-lisgis-constitutional-threshold) the director general and his statisticians to justify the population benchmarks behind a proposed expansion of the chamber from 73 to 87 seats.
qualifier: 2004 Act in force; independence and coordination provisions not shown in rows

summary: The telecommunications regulator continues to refuse to publish what the gateway monitoring system earns ([report](2026-08-31-smartnewsliberia-lta-revenue-disclosure-pressure)).
developments:
The telecommunications regulator's board chairman again declined to say what the international gateway monitoring system has earned, and the dispute has acquired a legal edge ([report](2026-08-31-smartnewsliberia-lta-revenue-disclosure-pressure)).

2026-09-06 - the Act was enforced against agencies for the first time in the repository's record: the information commission and a transparency organisation [ran compliance visits from 11 August to 2 September 2026 covering the national identification registry, the statistics institute, the community empowerment agency and the water and sewer corporation, with three further agencies scheduled for 8 to 10 September](2026-09-06-liberia-iic-cental-foi-compliance-drive). No findings, compliance scores or enforcement actions from the round are published, and it is a partnership exercise rather than a statutory inspection regime.
qualifier: unplaced: mapped row shows only LTA disclosure refusals; the FOI Act 2010 sits under include.access-foi-act

summary: The [telecoms regulator fined an operator LRD 4m](2026-07-22-liberia-strips-starcell-of-operating-license) for issuing a subscriber's module to a third party, the first privacy penalty on the record.
developments:
It was imposed by the telecoms regulator rather than under data-protection law, which had none in force at the time ([fine](2026-07-22-liberia-strips-starcell-of-operating-license)).

The reform package announced the same month does not name a data-protection function ([package](2026-07-17-lta-telecom-reforms-star-cell-revoked-fpa)), and no data-protection authority exists to which such a case could now be brought.
qualifier: privacy enforcement by the telecom regulator; no data protection authority constituted

summary: A [riders' union memorandum](2026-08-16-liberia-motorcycle-union-digital-liberia-mou) would build digital identity, satellite tracking and a rider database for commercial motorcycle operators, with no data-protection basis reported.
developments:
It was signed in August 2026 between the union and a private digital services company, aimed at curbing vehicle theft and linking informal-sector riders to formal financial and government services ([memorandum](2026-08-16-liberia-motorcycle-union-digital-liberia-mou)).

It is a private arrangement covering location tracking of a working population: no custodian, retention rule or consent mechanism is reported, and no statutory backing is claimed. It was signed three days before the country's first data-protection statute took effect.

Officials [posted spreadsheets of children enrolled in a donor-funded social protection programme to Facebook, with names, schools, home addresses and caregivers](2026-09-14-lbr-fpa-officials-post-vulnerable-childrens-data), reported on 14 September 2026; no response from the gender ministry or the funder is reported, and no action under the data-protection statute is held.
qualifier: unplaced: mapped row is a private rider registry; the Act in force sits under gov.protect-dp-bill

summary: [US$361,151.36 in arrears was waived](2026-08-03-liberia-atu-arrears-waiver-voting-rights) and voting rights restored at the continental telecommunications union in July 2026, after withholding dating to 1982.
developments:
Current obligations were arranged and the ratification instrument deposited ([waiver](2026-08-03-liberia-atu-arrears-waiver-voting-rights)).

Separately the central bank governor proposed shared cybersecurity standards, cross-border incident reporting and supervisory-technology adoption among West African regulators, citing the country's own instant-payment launch as a benchmark; nothing is adopted, funded or scheduled, and the proposal is one governor's rather than the college's position ([proposal](2026-08-19-liberianobserver-cbl-governor-cyber-resilience)).

2026-09-20 - the revenue authority [signed a memorandum to help its Gambian counterpart build a revenue collection dashboard on the model of its own](2026-09-21-gmb-gnnliberia-lra-gra-revenue-dashboard), [sending its dashboard's developer to Banjul for an initial three weeks](2026-09-21-gmb-thepoint-gra-lra-digital-cooperation-deal). It is peer assistance with no value stated.
qualifier: ATU voting rights restored; CSWAMZ cyber proposal is one governor's call with nothing adopted

summary: The [Standards Authority Act](2022-08-05-liberia-act-establishing-liberia-standards-authority) grounds the apex standards body expressly in ECOWAS quality-infrastructure instruments.
developments:
The [2022 Act](2022-08-05-liberia-act-establishing-liberia-standards-authority) creating the Liberia Standards Authority cites the ECOWAS quality infrastructure — ECOQUAL, ECOSHAM and Regulation C/REG.19/12/13 — and World Trade Organization technical-barriers obligations as its grounding, which is regional legal harmonisation done through domestic enactment.

The [February 2026 entry](2026-02-20-liberia-ghana-sierra-leone-ecowas-free-roaming-agreement-lta) into the ECOWAS free roaming agreement with Ghana and Sierra Leone is the other harmonisation step the repository holds, with the regulator stressing that full implementation still had to follow.

2025-12-01 - banking identity is the third harmonisation track: the [African Development Fund approved a US$8m grant in 2023 for a West African Monetary Institute project to harmonise bank customer identification across four West African Monetary Zone countries, Liberia among them](2025-12-01 Biometric Digital-ID in Africa - Ten Country Case Studies). No implementation stage, vendor or Liberian start date is stated.
qualifier: no REC cyberlaw instrument referenced or domesticated in the rows

summary: [Free roaming with two neighbours](2025-02-05-west-african-roaming-mou-lbr-gmb-sle) has run since May 2025, and spare fibre on a four-country power grid is agreed for commercialisation.
developments:
The roaming arrangement puts a home module at local rates across the three countries, with no traffic or price data published ([roaming](2025-02-05-west-african-roaming-mou-lbr-gmb-sle)).

Regional consensus was reached in June 2026 to commercialise spare fibre on the shared transmission grid across four countries, which would give the country its first terrestrial redundancy against sole reliance on one submarine landing; no operator, tariff or date is published ([grid fibre](2026-06-16-transco-clsg-fibre-expansion-techafricanews)).
qualifier: three-country free roaming in effect; no traffic reported; CLSG fibre not in service

summary: A rights organisation's reading puts the country [among three committing to hand over any data requested](2026-06-08-hrw-human-rights-assessment-afghs-bilateral-health-agreements) for an American audit without explicit privacy safeguards.
developments:
It is also among two whose data-sharing arrangement is deferred to an unpublished appendix, and outside the five whose text requires unilateral specimen and pathogen-sequencing sharing; the signed memorandum carries no specimen clause ([assessment](2026-06-08-hrw-human-rights-assessment-afghs-bilateral-health-agreements)).

The same reading names the country as lacking a binding comprehensive data-protection law, which is what makes the audit-access provision acute. That law has since been signed, and the appendix is still unpublished.
qualifier: rows hold only a health memorandum reading; no transfer rule on record

summary: [Executive Order 163](2026-04-28-liberia-executive-order-163-otdi-national-digitalization) creates a central standards authority and requires an interoperability framework within 180 days.
developments:
Before April 2026 no body owned government-wide technical standards. [Executive Order 163](2026-04-28-liberia-executive-order-163-otdi-national-digitalization) creates the Office of Technology, Digitalization and Innovation as that authority and requires a first release of the Government Interoperability Framework within 180 days, with an enterprise architecture framework and a digital systems inventory alongside.

The [chief technology officer's terms of reference](2026-07-17-liberia-otdi-terms-of-reference-executive-order-163) assign the drafting duty. Nothing has been published, so the standards themselves remain prospective.
qualifier: standards duty assigned to OTDI; nothing published by the as-at

summary: The [Liberia Standards Authority](2022-08-05-liberia-act-establishing-liberia-standards-authority) has been the apex national standards body since its enacting Act of August 2022.
developments:
The [Act](2022-08-05-liberia-act-establishing-liberia-standards-authority) signed 5 August 2022 creates the authority as the apex national standards body, grounded in the ECOWAS quality infrastructure and World Trade Organization technical-barriers obligations.

The repository holds no standards catalogue, no accreditation record and no conformity-assessment output from the authority since. The capture of the Act itself is an excerpt, the source scan having yielded only the preamble and enacting clause.
qualifier: standards authority established 2022; no ICT or data standards or quality policy on record

summary: [ePhyto](2026-04-21-liberia-launches-e-phyto-system-agricultural-trade) went live in April 2026, adding to the [numbering plan's](2023-12-01-liberia-lta-national-numbering-plan) adoption of ITU-T recommendations.
developments:
The [National Numbering Plan](2023-12-01-liberia-lta-national-numbering-plan) of December 2023 adopts ITU-T Recommendation E.164 for national number structure and E.212 for mobile country and network codes, giving an international standard domestic legal effect through the regulator.

In the window Liberia [launched the IPPC and FAO ePhyto exchange](2026-04-21-liberia-launches-e-phyto-system-agricultural-trade) on 20 April 2026 under the Regional ePhyto Africa Window, replacing paper phytosanitary certification with an internationally recognised digital certificate in support of the World Trade Organization trade facilitation agreement.
qualifier: ITU-T E.164 and E.212 adopted; ISO membership not on record

summary: The [2007 Act's](2007-01-01-liberia-telecommunications-act-2007) consultation duty is binding and was exercised twice in the window.
developments:
Sections 7(1) and 11(4) of the [Telecommunications Act 2007](2007-01-01-liberia-telecommunications-act-2007) require the ministry and the regulator to consult publicly and take account of the results before adopting policy or exercising authority likely to have substantial sector impact — the clearest binding consultation duty the repository holds.

It was exercised on [satellite communications guidelines](2026-02-23-liberia-lta-consultation-document-satellite-communications-guidelines) from 23 February 2026, with a public forum, a comment deadline and a published consultation report. Outside the telecommunications duty, a [two-day consultation](2025-11-14-liberia-national-data-policy-multistakeholder-consultation-au) in November 2025 brought civil society, academia, the private sector and the media into drafting the National Data Policy.
qualifier: statutory consultation duty exercised with published consultation report

summary: The [telecoms regulator's own revenue is unpublished](2026-08-04-lta-revenue-secrecy-raises-transparency-questions), a corruption complaint against it is under investigation, and the police answered a procurement question with a denial.
developments:
Its licensing fees, spectrum charges, regulatory levies and numbering receipts are not published, nor is an audited account of them ([revenue secrecy](2026-08-04-lta-revenue-secrecy-raises-transparency-questions), [alarm](2026-08-03-revenue-secrecy-at-lta-raises-alarm)).

A complaint over the replacement traffic-monitoring arrangement was forwarded to the anti-corruption commission's investigation unit on 30 July 2026, with no evidence publicly produced and no findings made ([complaint](2026-07-30-liberia-lacc-weighs-investigation-into-lta)).

The national police stated in August 2026 that no facility uses satellite internet and that connectivity comes from the state operator under an institutional contract, and confirmed buying used vehicles from an American firm; no contract, value or procurement record is published alongside the denial ([statement](2026-08-22-liberia-lnp-starlink-vehicle-procurement-fpa)).
qualifier: unplaced: press debate of LTA revenue on record but no published policy documents among mapped rows

summary: The [Universal Access Fund](2015-09-01-liberia-lta-universal-access-fund-regulations-reg-0006) levy of 0.5 per cent of licensee revenue remains the only standing domestic mechanism.
developments:
[LTA-REG-0006](2015-09-01-liberia-lta-universal-access-fund-regulations-reg-0006) sets the licensee contribution at 0.5 per cent of annual gross revenues, allows extraordinary contributions including national-budget allocations, and requires annual legislative approval for disbursement and audited accounts. Its most recent published deployment is a [satellite installation in Vahun District](2025-10-20-liberia-uaf-starlink-installed-vahun-district-lofa), Lofa County.

The wider fiscal space moved in the window rather than the digital allocation: [the general services tax rose from 12 to 13 per cent](2026-04-07-liberia-lra-adjustment-goods-and-services-tax-rates) from 1 May 2026 under the Tax Amendment Act, a prior action the [Fund's third review](2026-04-07-liberia-imf-country-report-26-98-third-ecf-review-rsf) records as closing a US$10m gap for the 2026 fiscal year. No digital line is identified inside it.
qualifier: universal access fund levy in regulation with deployments published; no budget execution report held

summary: The [Cybaston five-year framework](2024-09-24-liberia-cybaston-five-year-digital-fast-track-agreement) is the standing vendor relationship; three further partnerships were signed in the window.
developments:
The [master service framework signed 23 September 2024](2024-09-24-liberia-cybaston-five-year-digital-fast-track-agreement) covers undersea capacity of up to 1 Tbps, a data centre for consolidated e-government services, e-visa, e-tax and e-tourism, a security operations centre and an incident response team, with handover to the ministry in September 2029.

Added since: a [UNDP and operator memorandum](2025-11-05-undp-orange-liberia-mou-digital-transformation-youth) of 5 November 2025 on digital skills, innovation hubs and inclusion beyond Monrovia, with no value stated; a [five-year United States memorandum](2025-12-09-liberia-mofa-us-liberia-health-cooperation-mou) of 9 December 2025 committing US$124,418,400, with integrated digital health information systems named as one funded line; and Liberia's [first Digital Village](2026-05-26-liberia-digital-village-program-lofa-huawei-partnership) in Lofa County with Huawei, for which no signed instrument, value or duration is published.

summary: A [youth entrepreneurship investment bank](2026-07-28-liberian-observer-24-hour-digital-economy-national-switch) is put at almost US$18m targeting 30,000 businesses and about 100,000 jobs, with no disbursement stated.
developments:
A national coordinator has been recruited and a board is being constituted ([the bank](2026-07-28-liberian-observer-24-hour-digital-economy-national-switch)).

It is the only domestic financing instrument in the repository outside the central bank's own regulations, and it is stated by a minister at a town hall rather than in an appropriation or a charter.
qualifier: no private digital commitment starting 2024–2026 on record

progress: Mixed, a US$50m regional credit was signed while the development bank cut digital from its country strategy
summary: [US$50m was committed](2026-06-08-125m-world-bank-wardip2-financing-techafricanews) for broadband, cybersecurity, digital governance and payments, while a bank strategy [cut its sectors from four to three](2026-07-31-liberia-afdb-country-strategy-paper-2026-2031), dropping digital.
developments:
The credit sits within a US$137m three-country operation and was signed in June 2026 as part of US$125m of agreements ([signature](2026-06-08-125m-world-bank-wardip2-financing-techafricanews), [operation](2026-03-13-techafricanews-world-bank-wardip2-137m)).

The bank strategy for 2026-2031 keeps transport, energy and skills with an indicative programme of UA 129m, 36.3 per cent unfunded, and no digital lending line ([strategy](2026-07-31-liberia-afdb-country-strategy-paper-2026-2031), [approval](2026-02-01 AfDB Liberia Country Strategy Paper 2026-2031)).

A US$30m identity and digital government project is running, with a US$2m tranche put on hold during the identity system's debt lock and no disbursement total published ([project](2025-03-24 Liberia launches DPI project (GREAT) with $30M World Bank funding), [commitment](2025-01-01-world-bank-lbr-2025-liberia-great-digital-id-bw03)).

2025-12-01 - a smaller regional grant reaches the identity layer of banking: [US$8m from the African Development Fund, approved in 2023, for a four-country bank identification and interoperability project run by the West African Monetary Institute](2025-12-01 Biometric Digital-ID in Africa - Ten Country Case Studies). No disbursement or Liberian share of it is held.

progress: Mixed, a dormant licence was revoked while a fifth-generation plan has no spectrum award behind it
summary: A [universal licence was revoked](2026-07-22-liberia-strips-starcell-of-operating-license) in July 2026 after six years without operation, leaving two mobile operators of any scale.
developments:
Spectrum, numbering and regulatory privileges reverted to the regulator, the licensee having been suspended for 90 days from February 2026; the market at mid-2026 is estimated at 3.2m subscribers for the leading operator, 2.3m for the second and 14,000 for the state operator ([revocation](2026-07-22-liberia-strips-starcell-of-operating-license)).

Fifth-generation services are stated as planned with investors still being engaged, and no spectrum award, licence condition or launch date is published ([plans](2026-01-29-liberia-verge-5g-revolution-observer)).

A continental governance index scores [mobile communications at 58.4 of 100 for 2023, 40th of 54 and up 8.6 points over the decade](2024-01-01-iiag-2024-profile-liberia), a composite reading rather than a subscriber count.
qualifier: modelled estimate; no survey figure in the 5 years to the as-at

summary: [1.84m internet users at 32.4 per cent of the population](2025-03-03 Digital 2025 - Liberia (DataReportal)) in early 2025, with about 3.8m offline and no later national figure published.
developments:
The reading is a commercial compilation rather than a regulator or statistics-office release ([penetration](2025-03-03 Digital 2025 - Liberia (DataReportal))).

Eighteen months on, no regulator subscription series, household survey or statistics-office chapter has replaced it, so the country's connectivity is measured once a year by an outside compiler.

A continental governance index gives a composite reading rather than a count, scoring [internet and computers at 21.4 of 100 for 2023, 44th of 54 and up 8.2 points over the decade](2024-01-01-iiag-2024-profile-liberia).
qualifier: modelled estimate; no survey figure in the 5 years to the as-at

summary: The [regulator's own series](2026-04-01-liberia-lta-sector-trends-at-a-glance-data-snapshot-2025) puts a 5GB basket at 12.1 per cent of monthly income in 2025, down from 13.6 per cent in 2023.
developments:
The [sector series](2026-04-01-liberia-lta-sector-trends-at-a-glance-data-snapshot-2025) holds the 5GB monthly basket flat at US$8 across 2023, 2024 and 2025 while average monthly income rose from US$59 to US$63 to US$66, giving affordability ratios of 13.6, 12.7 and 12.1 per cent against a 2 per cent benchmark. The whole of the improvement is income, not price.

Tax works the other way: the [April 2026 revenue notice](2026-04-07-liberia-lra-adjustment-goods-and-services-tax-rates) raises the general services rate to 13 per cent from 1 May 2026 while holding telecommunications at 15 per cent. Roaming charges among Liberia, Ghana and Sierra Leone were [removed in February 2026](2026-02-20-liberia-ghana-sierra-leone-ecowas-free-roaming-agreement-lta), with full implementation still to follow.
qualifier: published tariffs; no primary in the base

summary: The [domestic backbone is reported extending south-east](2026-07-23-liberia-lta-commissioner-honnah-expanding-digital-access) from one coastal city toward five counties, with no route map or kilometre figure.
developments:
The line is reported reaching a border town from the capital, with private firms extending it ([extension](2026-07-23-liberia-lta-commissioner-honnah-expanding-digital-access), [earlier account](2026-01-29-liberia-verge-5g-revolution-observer)).

No completion date is published, and the repository holds no national kilometre figure for the backbone at any date.
qualifier: extension under way; no route map or length figure published

summary: Two routes to a second landing are open: [one at Buchanan](2026-07-23-liberia-lta-commissioner-honnah-expanding-digital-access) sought with partial funding, and [an ECOWAS four-country cable approved at feasibility](2025-10-22-ecowas-segundo-cabo-submarino-validacao-estudo-cabo-verde).
developments:
2025-10-22 - member-state experts with their technical and financial partners [reviewed and approved the feasibility study for an ECOWAS second submarine cable serving Cabo Verde, Liberia, Sierra Leone and Guinea-Bissau](2025-10-22-ecowas-segundo-cabo-submarino-validacao-estudo-cabo-verde) at a workshop the ECOWAS Project Preparation and Development Unit convened in Monrovia; no route, cost, landing site or construction date is published.

2026-07-23 - the minister announced [a second submarine landing at Buchanan, with partial funding stated as sourced and investors still being sought](2026-07-23-liberia-lta-commissioner-honnah-expanding-digital-access) at a technology summit; no landing partner, cost or date is published. Neither record says whether the two are the same project.

The country has run on one landing in the capital, which is why the agreement to commercialise spare fibre on the regional power grid matters as much as the cable does: both would end sole reliance on a single route.

summary: The [exchange launched in 2015](2015-08-02-au-setting-up-and-launching-internet-exchange-point-liberia) is functional but [still under-peered](2025-12-05-liberia-lta-strengthen-internet-exchange-point-national-peering-forum) as at December 2025.
developments:
The Liberia Internet Exchange Point was [launched in Monrovia on 6 August 2015](2015-08-02-au-setting-up-and-launching-internet-exchange-point-liberia) by the African Union Commission with the ministry under the African Internet Exchange System project, which supplied equipment, technical support and capacity building. No separate licence or establishing regulation was located.

At the [national peering forum in December 2025](2025-12-05-liberia-lta-strengthen-internet-exchange-point-national-peering-forum) the regulator's commissioner said the exchange remains functional but suffers governance problems and limited provider participation, with many providers still not peering, against upgraded equipment and a newly elected association leadership.
qualifier: exchange functional but under-peered; no traffic or capacity cited

summary: [Satellite communications guidelines](2026-08-19-liberia-lta-satellite-communications-guidelines-pdf) were issued in August 2026 setting licensing, tax and service rules, with no licence yet issued under them.
developments:
The regulator frames the rules around national security and commercial transparency as space-based solutions become the route to territories terrestrial networks have not reached ([market rules](2026-08-25-liberia-regles-marche-telecoms-satellite-wearetech), [guidelines](2026-08-19-liberia-lta-satellite-communications-guidelines-pdf)).

It frames them as opening licensed satellite broadband to the named constellations ([framework](2026-08-19-liberia-lta-satellite-communications-framework)), and no licence has yet been issued on the record.
qualifier: regulator's guidelines issued August 2026; no licence issued under them on record

summary: The only published Liberian capacity figures are the [cable landing station's own rack specifications](2025-04-29-cable-consortium-of-liberia-co-location-services).
developments:
The [consortium's colocation page](2025-04-29-cable-consortium-of-liberia-co-location-services) offers climate-controlled racks at 2 to 10U at 1kW with a 2kW maximum, 24U at 3kW and 42U at 5kW at the Monrovia landing facility, with uninterruptible and generator power, air conditioning, fire suppression and cross-connect support.

These are offered configurations, not installed or occupied capacity, and no other Liberian facility owner publishes its own figures. What is being added is visible only through procurement: a [June 2026 tender](2026-06-09-liberia-moci-special-procurement-notice-ict-infrastructure-nsw) for eight application servers, four database servers and two storage arrays for the National Single Window.
qualifier: 0 of 3 multi-tenant facilities in service at Tier III or above

summary: A [national data centre was announced](2026-07-23-liberia-lta-commissioner-honnah-expanding-digital-access) in July 2026 to hold government data domestically, with no site, cost, timetable or operator named.
developments:
The announcement came from the posts and telecommunications minister ([announcement](2026-07-23-liberia-lta-commissioner-honnah-expanding-digital-access)).

A separate facility at Buchanan is stated as under development for sovereign hosting of the identity registry and the revenue authority, again with no cost or completion date published ([Buchanan facility](2026-03-01-liberia-national-data-governance-policy)); an operator [said in July 2025 it was building a Tier III+ data centre in Buchanan](2025-07-23-liberianinvestigator-orange-liberia-250m-buchanan-data-centre), and the sources do not say whether the two are one site.

Neither is the same project on the record, and the data governance policy that names the second sets a rule for data leaving the country that neither facility yet lets it obey.

The central bank [sought an owner's engineer in November 2025 for a purpose-built facility to house interbank payment and settlement operations](2025-11-17-cbl-reoi-lib-pss-head-office-facility), after [a US$3.9m grant received in March 2023 to upgrade its main and disaster-recovery data centres](2023-03-23-dcd-afdf-grant-liberia-payments-infrastructure). No award, site or completion of the upgrade is on record.

An older state project is held without an outcome: [the state operator said in July 2017 it was building a national data centre to host government data and applications](2017-07-30-frontpageafrica-libtelco-google-csquared-national-data-center), and no completion is on record.
qualifier: 2 of 3 multi-tenant facilities of known ownership nationally owned

summary: The [central bank's 2026 statement](2026-01-01-liberia-cbl-policy-statement-2026) undertakes minimum uptime, disaster-recovery and continuity standards for payment participants.
developments:
The [policy statement](2026-01-01-liberia-cbl-policy-statement-2026) commits the bank to establishing minimum uptime, disaster recovery and business continuity standards for payment participants and to requiring regular cybersecurity and operational resilience testing, alongside prefunding and settlement risk controls. It is the clearest regulatory step on continuity the repository holds for banks, mobile money and the national switch.

Against that, the supreme audit institution's own [2026-2030 plan](2026-07-01-liberia-gac-strategic-plan-2026-2030) records its information technology infrastructure as fragile, with gaps in servers, networks, backup systems and cybersecurity — a dated self-reported backup deficit at the body that audits everyone else.
qualifier: only central bank continuity standards planned; no government backup site on record

summary: The [WARDIP-SOP2 safeguards framework](2025-12-11-liberia-mopt-wardip-sop2-esmf) is the only Liberian document setting water and power rules at digital sites.
developments:
The [environmental and social management framework](2025-12-11-liberia-mopt-wardip-sop2-esmf) issued in December 2025 sets construction water-use and electrical-hazard requirements for data-centre and cable landing-station works under the regional digital integration project.

It governs construction, not operation: the repository holds no dedicated power or water provision figure for any Liberian data centre, and the [appraisal of the governance project](2024-05-07-liberia-worldbank-great-project-appraisal-document) extending the National Data Center carries none either.

summary: The [electricity regulator's 2024 report](2025-02-01-liberia-lerc-annual-report-2024) is the standing account of generation, imports, assets and connections.
developments:
The [annual report for 2024](2025-02-01-liberia-lerc-annual-report-2024) sets out installed against available generation, imports, transmission and distribution asset inventory, connections and peak demand, together with the non-compliance notices the regulator issued that year.

Added capacity is financed but not yet delivered: the government records [a further US$57m secured in March 2026](2026-03-01-world-bank-lbr-2026-mount-coffee-solar-expansion) to expand solar generation at Mount Coffee from 20 to 30 MW and add a 12 MW battery storage system.

The utility [runs a dry-season deficit from December to April and covers it with imports, about 50 MW by 2025 against 27 MW contracted in 2022](2025-05-27-wb-blog-liberia-electricity-utility-outlook). How exposed that leaves the grid showed in February 2025, when the Ivorian supplier [cut deliveries from 50 MW to 7.5 MW, widening load shedding in Monrovia while low water held back the Mount Coffee hydropower plant](2025-02-07-liberia-power-shortage-cote-divoire).
qualifier: survey figure; no primary in the base

summary: The [2015 Electricity Law](2015-10-23-liberia-2015-electricity-law) puts the rural energy agency and its fund on a statutory footing.
developments:
The [Act of 23 October 2015](2015-10-23-liberia-2015-electricity-law) amends the public authorities law to establish the Rural and Renewable Energy Agency and the Rural Energy Fund and requires the agency to file system plans with the regulator.

The repository holds no rural connection series against it. The [electricity regulator's 2024 report](2025-02-01-liberia-lerc-annual-report-2024) publishes connections and peak demand nationally without a rural split.

National access is measured where the rural share is not: the World Bank puts [access at 32.5 per cent after doubling over the decade to 2024, with rural access disproportionately low](2025-05-27-wb-blog-liberia-electricity-utility-outlook), against a compact target of [75 per cent by 2030 through 100,000 household connections a year](2025-05-27-wb-blog-liberia-electricity-utility-outlook).
qualifier: survey figure; no primary in the base

summary: The [telecoms traffic-monitoring concession is suspended](2026-07-30-liberia-lacc-weighs-investigation-into-lta), with operator funds in escrow of undisclosed amount and a corruption complaint under investigation.
developments:
A joint legislative committee recommended renegotiation rather than cancellation; the original concession was ratified by the legislature in 2022 and held valid by the justice ministry in 2024 ([suspension](2026-07-30-liberia-lacc-weighs-investigation-into-lta)).

No evidence has been publicly produced and no findings made in the complaint, so a revenue-assurance system for the whole telecoms sector is off while the arrangement that would replace it is contested.
qualifier: only a telecom traffic-monitoring concession held; nothing on core government systems

summary: [Procurement staff from 56 entities](2026-05-12-liberia-ppcc-egp-phase-ii-training-of-trainers) began in-house training in May 2026 on a platform still facilitated by its vendor.
developments:
A [two-week training of trainers](2026-05-12-liberia-ppcc-egp-phase-ii-training-of-trainers) began on 11 May 2026 for procurement staff and technicians from 56 entities already onboarded to the electronic procurement platform, following a first phase covering six pilot ministries. The platform is still facilitated by its vendor.

The strongest evidence of in-house build capacity is elsewhere: the [online police clearance platform](2026-05-04-liberia-lnp-lra-online-police-clearance-platform-gnn) that went live on 1 May 2026 was written by revenue authority programmers rather than procured.
qualifier: revenue authority programmers built the platform; no systematic programme or IT cadre on record

summary: The [cybersecurity strategy](2024-07-01-liberia-national-cybersecurity-strategy-2025-2029) is published and its scheduled council, act and operational deliverables are all unheld two years past their dates.
developments:
Its action plan dated deliverables from the fourth quarter of 2024; the cover reads July 2024 for a 2025-2029 period while every running header reads a draft for 2024-2029, and whether the posted file is the adopted final text is not established from the document ([strategy](2024-07-01-liberia-national-cybersecurity-strategy-2025-2029)).

The national cybersecurity council it scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2024 has no constituting instrument, membership or meeting record; the repository holds no record of establishment rather than a stated non-delivery.

A House investigation was ordered in February 2026 into an alleged breach of about 2m citizens' data across the revenue, electricity and insurance bodies, with no findings published; the revenue authority denied the breach, and the probe cited the absence of a national cybersecurity strategy ([investigation](2026-02-12-house-probe-data-breach-2m-citizens-observer)).
qualifier: strategy published but adoption not established; council not constituted

summary: The [Government Service Bus](2025-11-06-liberia-great-project-implementation-status-results-report-seq3) carried zero of a target ten systems at September 2025, and its prototype package was re-tendered.
developments:
The [implementation report of November 2025](2025-11-06-liberia-great-project-implementation-status-results-report-seq3) puts the indicator for government systems exchanging data through the new service bus at zero as at 30 September 2025, against a target of ten by December 2030.

The [revised procurement plan of 13 February 2026](2026-02-13-liberia-great-project-procurement-plan) shows the prototype design and installation consultancy listed twice: the firm-based package cancelled, and an individual-consultant package pending implementation from 25 February 2026. The shared digital infrastructure consultancy at the National Data Center was signed on 6 October 2025.
qualifier: service bus prototype re-tendered; zero systems connected

summary: A [joint directive of February 2026](2026-02-16-liberia-fia-cbl-directive-additional-cdd-measures-non-resident) binds financial institutions to identity verification for non-resident customers.
developments:
[Directive CBL/FIA/001/2025](2026-02-16-liberia-fia-cbl-directive-additional-cdd-measures-non-resident), signed jointly by the financial intelligence agency and the central bank on 16 February 2026 and effective immediately, requires additional customer due diligence for non-resident, non-Liberian customers, addressing a deficiency named in the 2023 regional mutual evaluation.

The general obligation is older: [Executive Order 147](2025-04-01-liberia-executive-order-147-mandatory-nbis-enrollment) requires every public and private institution to verify against the registry. What that dependency costs when the register stops was visible in July 2026, when the Senate [summoned the registry](2026-07-03-liberianobserver-national-id-crisis-resurfaces-on-senate-floor) over more than six months of suspended card issuance while regulated institutions refused expired cards for banking and mobile money.

The tax system was an earlier user: the revenue authority [linked its integrated tax administration system to the identity registry to verify national IDs during fiscal year 2023](2024-06-30-lra-2023-annual-report), before the executive order made verification general; no verification volume is published.
qualifier: tax system verifies national ID on the revenue authority's account; no usage published

summary: A [national sample referral framework](2026-07-01-liberia-moh-validates-integrated-sample-referral-system-framework) was validated in July 2026; the health information system is rated [early maturity](2026-05-01-who-liberia-annual-report-2025).
developments:
A [World Health Organization-supported functionality assessment](2026-05-01-who-liberia-annual-report-2025) rates the health information system at overall early maturity, with harmonisation and interoperability named as work still to be done; 137 mobile phones and 31 laptops were supplied to strengthen electronic surveillance reporting.

In July 2026 the ministry [validated a framework](2026-07-01-liberia-moh-validates-integrated-sample-referral-system-framework) linking laboratory sample transport, results reporting and disease surveillance. It was validated, not adopted: the ministry states adoption and implementation remain prospective.
qualifier: sample referral framework validated; adoption and implementation prospective

summary: A [costed roadmap](2025-09-10-liberia-moe-au-iped-emis-modernisation-roadmap) introduces national learner and teacher identifiers; the [2025/26 census](2026-03-30-liberia-moe-launches-2025-2026-national-school-census) moved to digital collection.
developments:
The [peer review](2025-09-02-liberia-au-iped-emis-peer-review-report) records a stalled transition from a paper first-generation system to a digitised second, with limited integration across sub-sectors, weak legal frameworks, data gaps since 2022 and a proposed three-year US$4.5m action plan.

A [three-year modernisation roadmap](2025-09-10-liberia-moe-au-iped-emis-modernisation-roadmap) validated 1-5 September 2025 introduces national unique learner and teacher identifiers for integration and traceability, and the [2025/26 national school census](2026-03-30-liberia-moe-launches-2025-2026-national-school-census) ran on school-based digital collection across all 15 counties and 125 districts from 27 March 2026.
qualifier: EMIS roadmap introduces learner and teacher identifiers; no exchange in service

summary: [Registry integration with other national systems](2025-07-28-world-bank-realise-p174417-isr-seq9-liberia-household-social-registry) is recorded as ongoing, with no system named as connected.
developments:
The [implementation report of July 2025](2025-07-28-world-bank-realise-p174417-isr-seq9-liberia-household-social-registry) puts the household social registry at about 442,000 records and states that registry enhancements and integration with other national systems remain ongoing.

The [independent completion review](2024-09-09-world-bank-ieg-icr-review-liberia-social-safety-nets-p155293) of the earlier project describes what was built — the registry plus an integrated system with enrolment, payment, monitoring, grievance-redress and access-management modules, held by the gender and social protection ministry. No connection to the identity register or to any other national system is recorded as live.
qualifier: registry-backed transfers delivered through mobile money; no ID linkage on record

summary: Card issuance was [suspended for more than six months](2026-07-03-liberianobserver-national-id-crisis-resurfaces-on-senate-floor) while institutions continued to require the card.
developments:
In [March 2026 the Senate referred](2026-03-05-liberia-senate-inquiry-national-id-card-suspension) the suspension of national identity card issuance to committee and summoned the registry's leadership, on the ground that banks and other institutions treat the card as mandatory identification.

Four months later the [Senate summoned the registry again](2026-07-03-liberianobserver-national-id-crisis-resurfaces-on-senate-floor), unanimously, on the contradiction that the state had suspended issuance for more than six months while its own regulated institutions refused expired cards for banking and mobile money. The registry had earlier put arrears of US$1.7m owed to its systems vendor [on the record](2025-06-06-gnnliberia-nir-milestones-challenges-executive-order-147).

2026-09-08 - the replacement of the system is signed and cannot start. A [US$54.7 million concession with an Austrian supplier is signed but implementation cannot begin until legislative ratification and other legal requirements are completed, the identification registry's executive director said](2026-09-08-lbr-nir-oesd-digital-id-concession). The project as described covers biometric enrolment and deduplication, digital and physical credentials and an integrated identity platform beyond cards. No signature date is stated, so no deal record was built, and no legislative timetable, concession term or data-custody arrangement is published.

2026-09-16 — the registry [appealed to the legislature to ratify the US$54.7m build-operate-transfer agreement with its Austrian supplier](2026-09-17-lbr-newdawn-nir-appeals-legislature-oesd-bot-ratification); nothing can start until it does.
qualifier: issuance suspended over a year; replacement sought at US$39m

summary: Mass enrolment has been [suspended since June 2025](2026-08-18-liberia-ppp-digital-id-osd) on coverage below 15 per cent, with a concession to enrol all 5.3m people now before Parliament.
developments:
The concession is with an Austrian firm to finance enrolment in 18 months, operate and transfer; consultations have concluded and the draft agreement has gone to Parliament, with selection and terms unpublished until legislative approval completes and the registry stating it will disclose the agreement only after ratification ([concession](2026-08-18-liberia-ppp-digital-id-osd), [firm](2026-08-17-liberia-biometric-id-austrian-firm-ppp), [restart](2026-05-28-osd-concession-issuance-restart-biometricupdate)).

About 740,000 had enrolled by the end of 2024 at a US$5 card fee, and about 640,000 prior registrants were locked out with issuance halted ([lockout](2026-03-20-national-id-rollout-held-up-1-7m-debt-fpa)); no updated enrolment figure has been published ([lockout](2026-03-20-national-id-rollout-held-up-1-7m-debt-fpa), [funding gap](2025-06-09 Liberia needs more funding to widen national ID coverage (NIR's Peters))).

Enrolment has been mandatory for citizens and 90-day residents since April 2025 under an executive order making the identification number the primary credential for banking, health, education and telecoms ([order](2025-04-30 Liberia makes biometric ID mandatory — Executive Order 147), [no identity, no transaction](2025-04-30-no-national-id-no-transaction-eo147-observer)).

So a mandatory credential has been unobtainable for more than a year, on a register the state cannot afford to run and is now handing to a concessionaire.

2026-09-16 — a presidential proclamation declaring National Identification Day [put enrolment at about 720,000](2026-09-16-lbr-apo-boakai-national-identification-day-proclamation), with issuance still suspended; the registry says [free cards under the pending US$54.7m agreement will go only to disadvantaged and unemployed citizens, others paying a fee](2026-09-17-lbr-allafrica-nir-free-id-cards-disadvantaged-only).

summary: The [driver licence and vehicle registry](2026-01-03-liberia-mot-adlvrs-driver-license-vehicle-registration-launch) moved onto a state-run platform rather than out to a concessionaire.
developments:
The [transport ministry's launch of January 2026](2026-01-03-liberia-mot-adlvrs-driver-license-vehicle-registration-launch) covers licence management, card printing, dispatch, audit trails and compliance monitoring on a state-run platform, with an online renewal application and billing integration to the revenue authority.

The identity register runs the other way. The [2011 Act](2011-08-08-liberia-national-identification-registry-act-2011) vests the biometric system in an autonomous state agency, but the registry's [arrears to its systems vendor were reported at US$1.7m](2025-06-06-gnnliberia-nir-milestones-challenges-executive-order-147) in June 2025, and the identity-document contract named in the Senate's [July 2026 debate](2026-07-03-liberianobserver-national-id-crisis-resurfaces-on-senate-floor) is a foreign supplier's.

Some enrolment capacity came from inside government rather than a vendor: the elections commission [transferred more than 500 biometric kits to the registry in July 2025 to spare a new purchase, subject to licensing and technical modification](2025-07-03-nec-hands-over-biometric-kits-to-nir). No record shows them in service.
qualifier: state-run licence platform; contracts and funding model not on record

summary: [Executive Order 147](2025-04-01-liberia-executive-order-147-mandatory-nbis-enrollment) mandates verification through an Identity Query Portal and an e-Verification platform.
developments:
The [order](2025-04-01-liberia-executive-order-147-mandatory-nbis-enrollment) requires all public and private institutions to use the registry database, the Identity Query Portal and the e-Verification platform, with data handling bound to Part IX of the 2011 Act. It is the only general authentication mandate the repository holds.

What the repository does not hold is any measure of use: no query volume, no participating-institution count and no availability figure for either service. The [suspension of card issuance](2026-07-03-liberianobserver-national-id-crisis-resurfaces-on-senate-floor) through the first half of 2026 makes that absence material.
qualifier: e-verification portal mandated for all institutions; no usage on record

summary: A [UNICEF-funded pilot](2025-01-21-liberianinvestigator-nir-national-id-documents-children-under-six) issues identity documents to under-sixes in three counties, free to parents.
developments:
The registry [changed its system in June 2023 to issue unique identification numbers to children under six](2025-01-21-liberianinvestigator-nir-national-id-documents-children-under-six), and a UNICEF-funded [pilot was inaugurated on 16 January 2025](2025-01-21-liberianinvestigator-nir-national-id-documents-children-under-six); by the registry's March 2025 account the pilot [dated from September 2023 and had enrolled 5,000 children in Montserrado, with Grand Bassa and Gbarpolu to follow](2025-03-11-fpa-nir-digital-transformation-partnerships-enrollment).

It [pilots in Montserrado, Grand Bassa and Gbarpolu, funded by UNICEF for an initial 5,000 children at no cost to parents, with the health ministry issuing free birth certificates alongside](2025-01-21-liberianinvestigator-nir-national-id-documents-children-under-six). The fee is the reason it exists: [ordinary enrolment carries a US$5 charge that put registration out of reach](2025-01-21-liberianinvestigator-nir-national-id-documents-children-under-six).

No national rollout, budget line or successor cohort is on the record.
qualifier: under-six identity numbers piloted in three counties

summary: A [point-of-birth pilot](2025-10-28-world-bank-digital-liberia-week-2025-event-book) links birth certificate, identity number and immunisation record; integration remains a stated priority.
developments:
The [identification session at Digital Liberia Week](2025-10-28-world-bank-digital-liberia-week-2025-event-book) in October 2025 carried the results of a UNICEF-supported pilot integrating birth registration with the national identity system, with the registry's executive director and UNICEF's chief of child protection setting out a point-of-birth workflow linking birth certificate, national identity number and immunisation record.

In [July 2026 the health ministry](2026-07-18-liberia-moh-crvs-decade-progress-registrar-generals-meeting) named interoperability with the identity registry among its civil-registration priorities for 2026-2036. Those are objectives rather than achieved conditions, and no national link is recorded as live.

The identification registry [plans one NID-CRVS system linking national identity with civil registration and vital statistics under the proposed US$54m partnership](2026-09-14-liberia-nid-crvs-link-osd-ppp-biometricupdate), signed but awaiting parliamentary approval. Nothing of it is built.
qualifier: point-of-birth linkage piloted; interoperability a 2026-2036 objective

summary: [Module registration was tied to the identity number](2024-10-10 Liberia sets July 2025 deadline for SIM registration linked to national ID (LTA-NIR MoU)) with a July 2025 deadline, and no compliance figure or enforcement action has followed.
developments:
The deadline was set under an October 2024 memorandum between the telecoms regulator and the identity registry ([memorandum](2024-10-10 Liberia sets July 2025 deadline for SIM registration linked to national ID (LTA-NIR MoU))).

No revised deadline is published either, on a register whose issuance was halted for most of the period the deadline ran, so the requirement and the credential it requires were unavailable at the same time.

The civil service uses the register for its payroll: under a [memorandum signed in May 2024](2024-05-28-csa-nir-mou-service-delivery) the Civil Service Agency [verifies government employees through the registry's e-verification portal and carries identity numbers on their work cards](2025-03-11-fpa-nir-digital-transformation-partnerships-enrollment), and the registry [reported ghost names removed from the payroll by March 2025](2025-03-11-fpa-nir-digital-transformation-partnerships-enrollment) without publishing a count.
qualifier: civil service payroll verified against the registry; no reconciliation across registers

summary: A [directive of September 2025](2025-09-23-cbl-directive-002-2025-routing-government-payments-neps-iips) routes all government mobile-money payments and collections through the national switch.
developments:
[Directive CBL/E-GOV/DIR/002/2025](2025-09-23-cbl-directive-002-2025-routing-government-payments-neps-iips) requires every government payment to a beneficiary by mobile money — salaries, pensions, social benefits and other transfers — to route exclusively through the national switch from 27 October 2025, and all revenue collections by mobile money from 1 December 2025.

The bank's [2025 annual report](2026-03-31-cbl-annual-report-2025) sets out the rest of what it governs: the payment system section, the regional settlement system, the instant payment system and mobile money, with a first series of cross-border transfers terminating into mobile wallets. Its [2026 policy statement](2026-01-01-liberia-cbl-policy-statement-2026) adds continuity and resilience testing obligations for participants.
qualifier: central bank directs government payments through its switch; no consumer-protection function on record

summary: Government-to-person mobile payments have routed [exclusively through the national switch](2025-09-23-cbl-directive-002-2025-routing-government-payments-neps-iips) since 27 October 2025.
developments:
The [directive](2025-09-23-cbl-directive-002-2025-routing-government-payments-neps-iips) names salaries, pensions, social benefits and other transfers, with settlement into the central account. The [governor's launch remarks](2025-12-17-cbl-eg-saamoi-special-remark-iips-launch-december-2025) of 16 December 2025 set out what the instant payment platform is to carry, including government-to-person payments, as the first phase of the national switch.

The largest live government-to-person flow runs outside it on an operator rail: the social protection project reports [over 15,000 households paid and more than L$1 billion disbursed](2026-01-27-liberia-realise-boakai-annual-message-cash-transfer-disbursement), delivered through mobile money, against a scheduled project closure in late 2026 with no successor named.
qualifier: social transfers paid over mobile money; salaries and pensions not shown digital

summary: A [mobile-money tax platform](2025-07-23-lra-orange-ecobank-integrated-mobile-money-tax-platform) carries taxes and fees for 18 ministries over USSD without internet.
developments:
The [platform launched in July 2025](2025-07-23-lra-orange-ecobank-integrated-mobile-money-tax-platform) connects directly to the integrated tax administration system and carries taxes and fees for 18 ministries and agencies over USSD with a text-message receipt, so it works without a data connection. It predates the central bank's routing mandate.

From [1 December 2025 all revenue collections by mobile money](2025-09-23-cbl-directive-002-2025-routing-government-payments-neps-iips) must route through the national switch. A [compliance audit covering 2018 to 2024](2026-05-20-mfdp-lra-cbl-joint-press-conference-gac-revenue-collection-audit) found variances between bills and payments in the customs and tax systems, discrepancies between the tax system and the general revenue account, and unauthorised withdrawals in transitory accounts.
qualifier: mobile money tax payment for 18 agencies; customs and electronic share not on record

summary: The state auditor found [US$36,768 paid in full](2026-08-11-liberia-gac-audit-undelivered-digital-lending-platform) for a digital lending platform that was contractually due live in May 2025 and never deployed.
developments:
The field verification was in May 2026 and the management letter issued in June ([audit](2026-08-11-liberia-gac-audit-undelivered-digital-lending-platform)).

The same audit found no functional project audit committee, a US$27,000 consultancy let without competitive procurement, and an agriculture commercialisation fund reporting dashboard never formally handed over to the ministry ([audit](2026-08-11-liberia-gac-audit-undelivered-digital-lending-platform)).
qualifier: unplaced: mapped row is an undelivered lending platform; the e-procurement platform sits under dpi.govtech-egp

summary: An [inclusive instant payment system](2026-08-16-africanenda-liberia-instant-payment-system-73-days-webinar) launched in December 2025 in 73 business days, interoperable between the two mobile-money networks.
developments:
It covers person-to-person and government-to-person payments, where mobile money had been split between two closed networks ([launch](2025-12-17-cbl-launches-iips-mobile-money-silos-fpa), [system](2025-12-16-liberia-launches-iips-techafricanews)).

The central bank's own account is that it was built to a business case rather than to a regulation and sequenced government payments first, moving civil-servant salaries off cheques into wallets and so giving the integrated operators access to float, against a national target of 50 per cent of adults holding an account ([central bank account](2026-08-16-africanenda-liberia-instant-payment-system-73-days-webinar)).

A national electronic payment switch is named as the follow-on, alongside person-to-government payments, with no go-live date or budget line published ([switch](2026-07-28-liberian-observer-24-hour-digital-economy-national-switch), [expansion](2026-07-13 Liberia Expands Digital Finance)).
qualifier: two-operator interoperability with G2P; merchant and P2G payments and agent networks not on record

summary: [52 per cent account ownership with more than 11m wallets](2026-07-13 Liberia Expands Digital Finance) in 2024 is the repository's current statement, with no later figure published.
developments:
The reading is two years old ([account ownership](2026-07-13 Liberia Expands Digital Finance)).

It predates the instant payment system, the interoperable fee schedule and the movement of civil-servant salaries into wallets, so the one measure of uptake the repository holds is from before everything that would have moved it.

The central bank's assessment for its [2026-2030 inclusion strategy found account ownership up from about 36 to over 50 per cent of adults under the 2020-2024 strategy, with far fewer using their accounts](2026-04-23-cbl-nfies-financial-inclusion-workshop); no usage figure is published.

2026-09-16 — [the draft financial inclusion strategy was validated with its dependence on identity and business registries named](2026-09-16-lbr-fpa-cbl-financial-inclusion-id-business-registry); no launch date is set.
qualifier: survey figure; no primary in the base

summary: Liberia has been [live on the regional settlement system](2025-04-02-cbl-eg-saamoi-remarks-papss-rollout-financial-education-launch) since March 2025, with the central bank as settlement agent.
developments:
The [governor's remarks at the rollout of 27 March 2025](2025-04-02-cbl-eg-saamoi-remarks-papss-rollout-financial-education-launch) record Liberia live on the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System with the central bank as the national settlement agent.

The bank's [2025 annual report](2026-03-31-cbl-annual-report-2025) confirms implementation and the official launch in 2025, and publishes the first series of cross-border transfers terminating into mobile wallets — the repository's first evidence of cross-border value arriving in a Liberian wallet rather than a bank account.
qualifier: PAPSS live with the central bank as settlement agent; no corridor costs or volumes published

summary: A [central-bank-approved fee schedule](2026-08-05-africas-digital-payment-revolution-why-liberia-must-move-faster-on-inclusive-instant-payment-systems) caps interoperable charges at 1.0 per cent of value to US$2,000 and a flat US$25.00 above it.
developments:
The service is available 24 hours a day ([schedule](2026-08-05-africas-digital-payment-revolution-why-liberia-must-move-faster-on-inclusive-instant-payment-systems)).

The flat cap is regressive above about US$2,500 ([schedule](2026-08-05-africas-digital-payment-revolution-why-liberia-must-move-faster-on-inclusive-instant-payment-systems)), where it falls below 1.0 per cent of value and keeps falling, so the schedule protects small payments and cheapens large ones.

2026-09-05 - consumer protection moved out of the capital: the telecommunications regulator [opened its first service centre outside Monrovia, at Buchanan in Grand Bassa County, handling consumer complaints and community-radio compliance](2026-09-05-liberia-lta-decentralizes-consumer-services-buchanan). No staffing, opening hours, caseload target or programme of further centres is published.

Drafting of a [2026-2030 financial inclusion and education strategy began at a central bank workshop on 22 April 2026, after an assessment of its predecessor found consumer protection and financial capability the weakest areas](2026-04-23-cbl-nfies-financial-inclusion-workshop).
qualifier: central bank-approved fee cap only; no conduct rules or redress body on record

summary: The [2011 Act](2011-08-08-liberia-national-identification-registry-act-2011) makes the biometric system the population register in law; enrolment remains partial.
developments:
The [Act](2011-08-08-liberia-national-identification-registry-act-2011) creates the autonomous registry and gives it the biometric system, the card and the Social Security Number as the primary government identity number, which is the statutory basis for a population register.

Coverage has not kept pace. The registry put enrolment at [759,223 individuals, 14.6 per cent of an estimated 5.2 million](2025-06-06-gnnliberia-nir-milestones-challenges-executive-order-147), in June 2025 across 30 permanent centres, and the [presidential proclamation of September 2025](2025-09-15-liberia-mofa-national-identification-day-proclamation) cited 720,000. The registry is not a complete population register and no statutory alternative exists.
qualifier: biometric ID register built from enrolment only; issuance suspended

summary: A [Birth and Death Registration Policy 2026-2031](2026-08-11-liberianobserver-govt-sets-ambitious-health-reform-agenda-birth-death-policy) was launched in August 2026, superseding the 2017 policy.
developments:
The [2017 policy](2017-11-01-liberia-moh-birth-and-death-registration-and-certification-policy) placed birth and death registration under the health ministry's Bureau of Vital Statistics and Principal Registrar and stated plainly that the system had never been fully developed.

Its successor was [launched at the national health review conference of 4-6 August 2026](2026-08-11-liberianobserver-govt-sets-ambitious-health-reform-agenda-birth-death-policy), with no policy text, target or budget line reported. The ministry's own [statement of priorities for 2026-2036](2026-07-18-liberia-moh-crvs-decade-progress-registrar-generals-meeting) names expanding digital registration, improving cause-of-death reporting and interoperability with the identity registry — objectives, not achieved conditions.

Birth registration [runs on a DHIS2-based information system across 58 centres in all 15 counties, with the registration rate put at 66 per cent in 2019/20 against 4 per cent in 2007](2024-12-11-unicef-liberia-children-legal-identity). In 2019 it [worked from 15 centres in county urban districts keeping combined paper records, with online registration then being introduced](2019-01-01-crvs-liberia-snapshot).
qualifier: births on DHIS2 in all counties; no current coverage figure; new policy has no target

summary: A [national digital postal address rollout](2026-07-23-liberia-lta-commissioner-honnah-expanding-digital-access) is stated as begun across all fifteen counties, with no completion date or addressing standard published.
developments:
The statement was made at a technology summit in July 2026 ([rollout](2026-07-23-liberia-lta-commissioner-honnah-expanding-digital-access)).

Digital addressing is one of the eight priority areas of the national digital strategy, and this is the only delivery statement against any of them.
qualifier: postal address rollout stated as begun; no standard published

summary: An enhanced collateral registry launched, extended to immovable property ([notice](2026-08-27-cbl-enhanced-collateral-registry-public-notice)).
developments:
The central bank launched an enhanced collateral registry on 27 August 2026 under an amended secured transactions regulation, extending it to immovable property ([notice](2026-08-27-cbl-enhanced-collateral-registry-public-notice)) and presenting it as a way to curb duplicate claims and expand business credit ([report](2026-08-27-liberianinvestigator-liberia-launches-digital-collateral-registry-to-curb-duplicate)).
